steps.text: Mix together vinegar, soy sauce, garlic, honey, olive oil, black pepper, Worcestershire sauce, onion powder, salt, liquid smoke, and cayenne pepper in a medium bowl until marinade is well combined.
Place steaks in a shallow glass dish. Pour the marinade over steaks and turn to coat; rub marinade into meat for optimum flavor.
Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 1 to 2 days.
Preheat the grill for medium-high to high heat. Lightly oil the grill grate. Cook steaks on the preheated grill until hot, slightly firm, and lightly pink in the center, about 7 minutes per side.
An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read 140 degrees F (60 degrees C) for medium. Discard leftover marinade.

raw_recipe.headline: Savory Garlic Marinated Steaks
raw_recipe.description: This New York strip or rib-eye marinade uses balsamic, soy sauce, garlic, honey, liquid smoke, and Worcestershire to add incredible flavor to steaks.

video.description: Discover the secret to tender, flavorful, simply irresistible steaks. This video shows you how to make a savory, aromatic marinade that combines balsamic vinegar, soy sauce, and Worcestershire sauce with lots of minced garlic, honey, and spices. Bring the marinated steaks to room temperature before taking them to the grill.

review.reviewBody: OH MY WORD!!!!! This is sooooo good!!! The amazing part is we only had time to marinate half an hour!!! I poked the steak with a fork all over, laid it in a shallow dish & poured enough marinade to cover the top & overflow a little & rubbed it in. In 15 minutes I flipped it over & did the same to the other side. I only used half the marinade so I could let my husband use the rest for basting the last few minutes on the grill. This was sooo good I told my husband he needn't take me out to steakhouses (my absolute favorite!!) anymore - he can just grill our own at home!! We used T-bone steaks. I used about 1/8 c. balsamic and the rest white wine vinegar because I ran out of the balsamic. Both our company & us ate til' we couldn't eat anymore only because it was so good!! I served with salad, Grilled Corn on the Cob (also on this site), Greek Chicken Pasta (without the chicken - also on this site), & garlic bread. MmmMmm Good!!

Made this tonight and it was a huge hit!! My 4 1/2 year old went back for seconds! I followed the recipe exactly with the marinade but cooked it a little differently. I marinated two locally raised grass fed rib eyes, and three small rib steaks for only 3 hours, pan seared it first on the stove in my cast iron skillet on medium high heat with a little bit of olive oil and fresh butter for about 3 mins per side for the rib eyes and a little less time for the rib steaks, then transferred to the grill on low heat for a few more mins to finish cooking while basting with cooked down marinade that I added a bit of cornstarch to thicken. End result was a delicious and juicy steaks that everyone raved about! Thank you so much for a wonderful recipe!!!

Instead of cooking it right away I let the steak set out to come to room Temperture and then I put the rib eye whole sliced into a gallon bag I then poured the marinade over the steak. I used red wine,chopped garlic, chopped onions very small chopped. olive oil, soy sauce,Worcestershire sauce and 2 cups beef broth. Let this set in frig. for about 2 hrs. or more it will not hurt the meat if you let it set longer in frig. I then drained liquid and cut up steak in chunks so it would go father. then I added marinate to pan and added steak and chopped Mushrooms and more sliced onions. This was he best chopped steak I have ever had. We put it over egg noodles because we wanted something else beside potatoes or rice. You can also do chicken,pork chops, or other meat. just try this I cut down the salt because all the liquid I used had loys of salt in it.

We made this using an herb balsamic and truffle olive oil. I only marinated for 30 minutes before pan-searing the steaks. Then, I reduced the remaining marinade and served it as a dipping sauce on the side! It was amazing!

I doctored the recipe with a whole navel orange, grinded or zested, your choice, milk (helps tenderize) and a lil meat tenderizer. Marinated for a week and a half in freezer, then fridge to thaw. My wife bought me pecan shells. Soaked them for two days and added to fire like chips for flavor.

FANTASTIC! Made it for steak. This was my contribution to a communal dinner with certified Foody Friends! Got raves. Per other reviews, did reduce the soy and vinegar by about a fourth. I think it was a good decision. Could definitely marinate more than 24 hours. Might do 48 next time. I used the diced garlic from a jar because you need so much. I will make this again for sure.

Sorry folks when I made this 2nd review it deleted my picture of the Ribeyes from May 1st. So both reviews show the NY Strips. Review #2 We made it again last night. This time instead of using quarter inch 8oz Ribeyes we used half inch 8oz New York Strips. We cooked them over indirect heat. The thickness and cooking method was the trick. We have learned from our mistake and thoroughly enjoyed them. Perfect medium rare. SUGGESTION. We actually cooked 2 extra steaks so we could use them the next day.One we diced up for Steak and Egg breakfast Burritos then tonight we sliced the last one up and made Fajitas with Bell Peppers and Onions with Guacamole. The flavor of the steaks today was amazing in both meals. Our first review was on May 1st. REALLY WORTHWHILE! TIP you know your own grill so grill it your way. Thanks again Angie for the recipe. LOVES2COOK.
Amazing! I cooked mushrooms in poured off marinade with a little butter. Also Amazing

Made double the ingredients and used it to sautee mushrooms and onions. This was so good, I cannot imagine if we had marinated the night before. I also cut balsamic vinegar in half and substituted white wine, it went so fast, one of the kids literally stole my plate when I walked away from the table briefly. Served a a warm Italian bread layered with freshly shredded greyure cheese....youll have one happy (and plate stealing family)!

Tasted great however, this much marinade is more for like 4 steaks. I made three and it filled the dish after putting steaks in to marinate. I did not put in 2 TSP pepper - I put in 1.5 tsp. It just seemed like a lot of pepper.
Putting them on the grill in a few hours

I fixed this marinade and let my steaks sit for 24 hours, I did add a teaspoon of meat tenderizor as the steaks were very lean. I fixed this for company and every one enjoyed the nice extra beefy taste it added to
very tender center cut Rib Eye steaks. Definately the one I'll go to for all my beef recipes.

I marinated my steak in a FoodSaver bag for about 2 to 3 hours. All I could taste was sweet. Half of the balsamic vinegar I used was from Italy so it was on the sweet side. But, this recipe is way too sweet. The Worcestershire flavor stood out also so the steak was quite raisiny. I would not use this recipe ever again.

This recipe was good for what it is. I do like a vinegar taste and I could see this being used for certain things, but I felt like it wasn't the best for a steak and potatoes type of dinner. I could see it being used to make a steak taco with some slaw or for a Korean dish with some white rice and pickled vegetables.
I had leftover marinade in a jar and used on a pork tenderloin for 2-3 hours then grilled. It was amazing!!
I did this recipe exactly as written, but used it for lamb loin chops. It was the best marinade I have ever used for lamb.

I used this recipe to season my steak to have with my alfredo. I was out of cayenne but I subbed with chilli powder and added oregano. My fam raved about the steak. I will definitely use this recipe again.
